title: Classical Music and the Symphony
text: Western classical music refers to music produced in or rooted in the traditions of European music, including liturgical (religious) and secular music. The Classical period (approximately 1750–1820) saw the development of the symphony, sonata, and string quartet forms, with composers including Joseph Haydn, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, and Ludwig van Beethoven. Beethoven's nine symphonies, particularly Symphony No. 5 and Symphony No. 9 (featuring the 'Ode to Joy'), are cornerstones of the repertoire. Mozart composed over 600 works including 41 symphonies, 27 piano concertos, and operas such as Don Giovanni and The Magic Flute. The Romantic period (1820–1900) expanded the orchestra and emphasized emotional expression.
